Cc: ClearStream Ops <ops@clearstream.io>

Subject: Tolerance-band SLA calculation concern (maintenance overlap)

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Quick note following yesterday's incident: between ~11:03 and 11:09 PST our production writes to the Redwood-backed ingestion endpoint saw sustained 400/503 errors and median p95 latency spiked to ~1.2s (baseline ~80ms). We opened internal tickets and attached a sample of client request IDs in the PDF (clearstream_ticket_4871.pdf).

EdgeGrid (our CDN/edge partner) posted a maintenance window for 11:00–11:05 which they listed as a planned soft-restart. However our telemetry indicates the impact lasted ~6 minutes and materially affected our SLA for November. When we ran your portal's SLA calculator we were told the event fell within your "tolerance band" and was not counted as a creditable outage — that feels inconsistent with our user impact and the timing.

Can you:
- Confirm how the tolerance band is applied (window length, burst de-dup rules)?
- Share the probe-level timeline or the exact timestamps Redwood used to arrive at the non-credit decision?
- If EdgeGrid's maintenance extended beyond their declared window, will Redwood treat that as third-party exclusion or as Redwood-affecting uptime?

We'd like a determination and any interim mitigation while we evaluate the billing impact.

Thanks,
Clara Hsu
Head of Platform Operations, ClearStream
clara@clearstream.io

Attachment: clearstream_ticket_4871.pdf (sample request IDs and client traces)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Clara Hsu <clara@clearstream.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-18T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tolerance-band SLA calculation concern (maintenance overlap)

Hi Clara — thanks for flagging this and for the request IDs. I’m sorry ClearStream saw that user impact. We want to make sure we get the right timestamps and explain the tolerance-band behavior clearly. Short answers up front:

- "Tolerance band" in our SLA pipeline refers to a short-duration spike filter we apply before triggering an outage interval. It’s meant to avoid crediting transient microbursts under our latency/availability SLOs. The policy is not a blanket exclusion for customer-visible errors.
- We calculate with a rolling 120s window and a 30s minimum sustained degradation threshold for availability (i.e., a degradation must persist beyond 30s inside the rolling window to be treated as an outage). The final recorded outage is the union of windows exceeding threshold; third-party maintenance can be excluded if it’s clearly attributed and documented.

That said, I need to validate the exact probe timeline and raw request logs. Can you confirm whether the request IDs in clearstream_ticket_4871.pdf are representative (not sampled) and share any CDN-side timestamps you have? I’m attaching a snapshot of our preliminary SLO computation for that day (slo_computation_snapshot.csv) — review the column named "outage_flags" for what the pipeline saw.

Next steps:
- Marissa, can you pull the probe-level traces and the edge traceroutes for 11:00–11:12 PST and confirm the exact start/end we observed?
- Kimberly, please stand by for the billing/credit calc once we have timestamps sorted.

Clara — I’ll follow up with the precise interval and proposed next steps by end of day tomorrow.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Attachment: slo_computation_snapshot.csv (internal computation snapshot)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-19T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: ClearStream tolerance-band analysis and proposed credit

Sean / Kim — pulled the raw probe and edge traces for ClearStream between 10:58 and 11:15 PST. Key notes below (trace file attached: trace_edgegrid_20271118.txt):

Summary of findings:
- Redwood active probes (region: us-west-2) show elevated error ratio starting at 2027-11-18T11:03:12-08:00 and ending at 2027-11-18T11:09:18-08:00 (total duration 6m6s). HTTP 5xx rate rose to ~22% at the peak; median p95 latency across probes increased to ~1.1s.
- Our rolling-window algorithm uses a 120s window with a 30s sustained-threshold inside that window. The way the detector works: if >X% of samples within the 120s window exceed the availability threshold and the high period persists longer than 30s, we mark an outage. We also merge adjacent windows if gaps between flagged windows <60s.
- For this event, the detector flagged a degradation starting at 11:04:00 and ending at 11:08:30 (unioned windows after merge) — which yields a 4m30s outage recorded in the SLO system. The first ~48s of the observed 6m6s were classified as pre-threshold fluctuation under the rolling median, which is why the portal snapshot shows a shorter outage.

Proposed customer-facing position:
- Because EdgeGrid published a maintenance window (11:00–11:05), our standard policy is to attribute direct network-layer outages to the third party only if their own telemetry shows impact that matches our probe windows. EdgeGrid has not yet admitted extension. If EdgeGrid accepts their window extended, we treat the overlap as third-party-maintenance exclusion for the overlapping duration; otherwise it’s Redwood-service-affecting.
- Given the unioned outage we recorded (4m30s), and ClearStream's billing cycle, a fair interim credit would be 0.37% of November's Redwood charges (calculated by outage_seconds / seconds_in_month, prorated to their SLO). That’s slightly conservative; we can round to 0.4% if legal wants cleaner numbers.

Action items:
- Sean: send the probe windows and proposed interim credit to Clara and ask EdgeGrid for a definitive statement on their maintenance end time.
- Kim: prepare a draft credit note for accounting (0.37% and an instruction to hold off on automated credit until EdgeGrid responds).

Attachment: trace_edgegrid_20271118.txt (edge traceroute and probe timestamps)

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Quoted excerpt of our detection logic (for transparency):
"If rolling_120s.median_latency > avail_threshold AND consecutive_flagged_duration > 30s THEN mark_outage. Merge gaps < 60s."

To: support@edgegrid.net
Subject: RE: ClearStream maintenance impact

Hi all,

We investigated the maintenance job that was scheduled for 2027-11-18 11:00–11:05 PST. During a config push we observed an unexpected confluence of a route recompute and a cache invalidation that caused connections for a small fraction of origin IPs to stall. The intended window was 11:00–11:05 but the rollback took longer than expected and our internal telemetry shows elevated error counts until ~11:09:30 PST.

We accept responsibility for the extended impact and will:
- Mark the maintenance record as extended to 11:09:30 PST (official log attached to internal ticket EG-20271118-67).
- Issue a service credit to ClearStream through the normal marketplace channels and share a copy with Redwood if requested.

Apologies for the customer disruption — we’ll follow up with a postmortem and remedial controls for safer rollbacks.

Regards,
EdgeGrid Incident Response
incident-response@edgegrid.net

Provisionally, given EdgeGrid's acceptance, the event should be classified as third-party-maintenance for the overlapped portion (11:03:12–11:09:18). Sean, please confirm with ClearStream whether they accept a third-party credit from EdgeGrid or prefer Redwood-provided interim credit immediately.

—Sean (forwarding)

Attachment: EG-20271118-67 (EdgeGrid internal incident log, referenced above)
